bull.t: Revenue rebound and high gross margins
bull.b: The sharp revenue rebound and very high gross margin indicate meaningful economic potential in ProQR’s partnered and licensing-oriented model. If growth persists as programs advance, strong gross margins could provide substantial operating leverage once development spending and commercial scale improve.

The equity financing and resulting cash balance provide resources to fund multiple clinical programs over the medium term. A runway extending into mid-2028 reduces immediate financing pressure and supports continued development, milestone generation, and platform investment without relying solely on near-term capital access.

bull.t: Axiomer platform advancing into clinical validation
bull.b: Progression of an AI-discovered candidate into human testing, alongside reported improvements in RNA editing efficiency, strengthens evidence that Axiomer can generate differentiated programs. Additional clinical readouts and broader platform application could improve partnering appeal and diversify future development opportunities.

bear.b: ProQR remains far from break-even despite revenue improvement, so its current operations do not yet support themselves financially. Persistent net and operating losses can erode equity, constrain strategic flexibility, and require continued funding before clinical programs can produce durable commercial returns.

Meaningfully negative operating and free cash flow shows that research and clinical development consume considerably more cash than the business generates. Continued burn raises the importance of future financings, collaborations, or milestone receipts and could increase dilution or funding risk if programs take longer to advance.

bear.t: Reliance on collaborations before product commercialization
bear.b: The absence of marketed products leaves ProQR dependent on partner funding, licensing receipts, milestones, and potential royalties rather than recurring product sales. These sources can be uneven and contingent on development progress, while the company continues carrying substantial R&D costs ahead of commercialization.
